T: Miracles happen in the most unexpected places.
D: A death row guard in 1935 comes to believe the gentle giant on his block can heal, and that he never committed the crime he is set to die for.
P: Serve the meatloaf when John Coffey gets his last meal.
S: Mrs Edgecomb's cornbread with honey butter
Cornbread baked in cast iron, honey butter melting on the warm slices.

Heat a 23cm cast iron pan in a 220C oven with 20g of the butter in it. Whisk the dry ingredients with a good pinch of salt, then whisk in the buttermilk, eggs and 100g melted butter. Pour into the hot pan and bake until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Beat the soft butter with the honey and salt flakes and serve with the warm cornbread.
120g butter, plus 80g soft butter for the honey butter@Dairy
Cornmeal fried okra with comeback sauce
Cornmeal-fried okra with comeback sauce. A Cold Mountain supper.

Stir the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, hot sauce and a squeeze of lemon into a comeback sauce. Soak the okra in the buttermilk while you mix the cornmeal, flour, paprika and salt. Toss the okra in the cornmeal mix to coat well. Fry in batches in oil at 180C until crisp and golden, then drain and salt. Serve hot with the sauce.
Mr Jingles' pimento cheese and crackers
Pimento cheese with crackers, a snack small enough to share with a mouse.
Beat the cream cheese and mayonnaise until smooth. Fold in the cheddar, capsicum, paprika and hot sauce and season with pepper. Pile into a bowl and serve with the crackers and celery.
M: Last meal meatloaf with mash and gravy
Meatloaf with mash and gravy, the meal before John walks the Mile.

Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk, then mix with the mince, grated onion, egg, thyme and plenty of salt and pepper. Shape into a loaf on a lined tray, stir the tomato sauce, sugar and vinegar together and brush half over. Bake at 180C for 1 hour, brushing on the rest of the glaze halfway, then rest it. Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with half the butter and a splash of the milk. Fry the sliced onion in the rest of the butter until brown, stir in the flour, then whisk in the stock and simmer into gravy. Wilt the silverbeet in a hot pan, slice the meatloaf thickly and serve with the mash, gravy and greens.
1 brown onion, grated, plus 1 sliced for the gravy@Produce
W: Top Hat peach cobbler with vanilla ice cream
Peach cobbler with vanilla ice cream. His first picture show is Top Hat.

Toss the peaches with the brown sugar, cinnamon, cornflour and lemon juice in a baking dish. Rub the butter into the flour and caster sugar, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls of dough over the peaches, leaving gaps for the juice to bubble through. Bake at 190C until the topping is golden and the fruit is bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm with the ice cream.
K: Lime and sugar cooler over ice, the colour of the faded lime floor.
Heat the sugar and water with strips of lime peel until dissolved, then cool and strain. Squeeze the limes and stir the juice into the syrup. Pour over ice and mint in 4 glasses and top with soda.
